title: A Typical Laplace Incident
subtitle: From the moment the first drop of rain falls, you must never hesitate and never tire.

trails.title: Hive Mind
trails.description: Don't mess with bees—especially the arcane ones.

content.text:
Name: Ludwig
Department: Laplace Staff Committee
Reason: Out-of-body Experience (OBE)

Summary:
The patient recently suffered a severe episode of OBE during his research on Holiday Language. His consciousness has since fully recovered. However, his soul has now repeatedly transferred to his familiar without warning, accompanied by short-term memory loss, a weakened sense of reality, and distorted time perception. Prior records indicate the patient lacks sufficient awareness of the risks tied to OBE. Ongoing supervision and intervention are required. He also reports consuming an unidentified arcane substance resembling "honey." Its composition remains unknown and requires further analysis.

Symptoms:
Abnormal self-perception: disordered sense of time and gaps in memory.
OBE Duration: Episodes can last several hours, typically followed by short-term memory loss.

Experiment and Intervention Record:
Picrasma Candy (complementary medicine)
No significant improvement observed. The patient's only feedback concerned the taste.

Risk Assessment:
Relatively high, though the patient is showing signs of improvement. Ongoing observation is recommended, with particular attention to recurrence of the following:
1. Depersonalization-derealization disorder
2. Speech and language impairment
3. Assaulting colleagues without conscious awareness

Recommendations:
1. Extend medical observation period until symptoms subside.
2. Keep systematic records of the time, duration, and patient descriptions of each OBE.
3. Restrict the patient from high-intensity psychic research for the duration of the observation period.

Doctor's Note:
The patient has come to regard his OBE as perfectly normal. His nonchalance and near-total disregard for treatment lead me to believe that the rehab center's coffee machine, which requires weekly repairs, may actually be more "stable" than he is.

items.text: The substitute director immediately considers many possibilities: a lab accident, time travel, unstable alchemical elements ...
He pushes the door open and bursts inside.
Office, Laplace

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Mr. Ludwig, are you there?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: *cough* His office is even messier than mine.
Several shadowy birds rush toward him, trailing smoke and ash.
Who—are—you?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Seelentausch!
An incantation is cast. The raven familiars lose their arcane connection, fading into mist and disappearing from the cluttered office.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What on ... Great! My colleagues have finally driven me to madness. Took them long enough.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But just what the hell is going on here?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I told them the place needed a full renovation after that fire, but they didn't listen.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Excuse me, Mr. Adler.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: During my research on Holiday Language, my soul left my body for a period. Quite the spiritual adventure, I must say.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Since then, my soul has adopted a habit of transferring itself into my familiar at random. As you might imagine, it takes some getting used to—tends to muddle the memory a little too.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I was in the middle of sorting some files when it happened this time.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Concerning, to put it mildly. Perhaps you should have stayed at the rehab center longer.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Oh, no need to worry about me. I've had my share of research accidents. All part of the job.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: He takes a moment to straighten his collar.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: More importantly, Mr. Adler, have you made any progress on the arcane pigment investigation since our last meeting?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Be it from Institutum Lorentz or the Foundation investigator dispatched at our request.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I did receive a report from Ms. Latham two days ago. She has made contact with the local Vigiles Bureau.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Apparently, some arcanist criminal organization is operating an extensive smuggling ring within Mexico City. It's been hindering her investigation in a number of ways.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I worry for her safety. I do hope the Vigils look after her.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: My thought exactly. I've made clear that her own safety is top priority. She should be under the Vigils' protection now.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: While we're ruminating on the topic, there's something I feel needs clarification.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I had thought the pigment investigation was a request from the Staff Committee, but you're the only member who has shown any interest in its progress. The request came directly from you, didn't it?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Well deduced, Mr. Adler.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: You've heard about the conflict between the internal factions of the Foundation, I assume? Inevitably, its impacts have affected Laplace as well.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: After I awoke from my coma at the rehab center, Commissioner Pedra paid me a visit. He warned me that over half of the Staff Committee supports the proposal of a comprehensive policy reform at Laplace.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Should it pass, Laplace may lose its independence and become a full subsidiary of the Foundation.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: He asked me to join the Staff Committee and oppose this policy reform. I agreed.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Oh, I see. Then if Laplace develops enough groundbreaking "Storm" technologies before the Foundation does, we can turn the tables on them.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Indeed, it would give us better leverage, if nothing else.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: But we don't have much time on our hands.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Their Hawks are gaining support from more commissioners as we speak. For now, all I can do is delay the proposal's review process.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Tch, typical politics.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You once led the Plesetsk branch, Mr. Ludwig, and as I am sure you can see, I have never been one for matters of politics or leadership.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I was only appointed to maximize the chance of preserving and continuing Director Lucy's research.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That is to say, is there any chance we could bring Director Lucy back to Laplace?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Whether possible or not, our first step in either case will be to stop this policy reform.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: If Ms. Latham's investigation yields no significant progress soon, all we can do is wait for good news from Lorentz Butterfly.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I'm confident she'll bring us something. She's always been one step ahead.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You sound quite certain of her. But we know nothing about this Lorentz Butterfly aside from a few unorthodox papers and provocative letters.
The bird-headed scientist chooses to remain silent, but the cryptic response proves a poor choice when dealing with an expert cryptologist.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Wait a minute. Impossible!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You know who Lorentz Butterfly is, don't you?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Hmm. It was the year of 1999. At the time, I was a visiting professor at Cambridge University. There was a student in my class, far too brilliant for her exceptionally young age.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: The staff told me she wasn't an enrolled student. She simply came every week to attend my lecture.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I had intended to recommend her for admission, but, of course, the "Storm" disrupted everything.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I ended up leaving Cambridge and joining Laplace myself.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: After the second "Storm," I paid the university a visit and saw that young lady again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Are you saying she survived multiple "Storms" on her own?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Yes. Though she didn't share the details, I could tell she was hiding a secret, or running from some serious danger.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: She had an exceptional gift for the sciences. Naturally, I invited her to join Laplace.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But from what little we know of her, she's ... dangerous.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I trust you would not mistake me for an idealist, Mr. Adler.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Dangerous as she may be, we need her help, especially in times like these.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: That said, should she become completely out of control ...

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I hope to be her one and only victim.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You have done little to reassure me, Mr. Ludwig.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But perhaps you're right. We must keep pushing forward at any cost.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Everyone's so doggedly determined. It's time I also mustered the strength to stay the course.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I will continue to monitor Ms. Latham's progress.
